details:
Pyrochron — Explore satellite fire detections in context

Pyrochron helps researchers, analysts and land managers make sense of active-fire detections from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellites. It combines a historical monthly view of four study areas—Pantanal, Quebec, Valparaíso and Punjab—with a live mode where users draw a custom area and query available NASA FIRMS detections from the last seven days.

For historical analysis, Pyrochron places observations on a shared grid, offers two ways to compare satellite activity, and lets users explore seasonal patterns against a fixed 2012–2019 same-month baseline. The live view filters provisional records, groups some repeat VIIRS detections into approximate daily clusters, and displays the results on a map and chart. Users can also inspect source availability and export selected data.

In a 2020–2024 held-out comparison with MODIS, count-ratio adjustment reduced pooled VIIRS-to-MODIS count error from MAE 50.83 to 5.33 across 61,441 matched cell-month comparisons. These are aggregate count-agreement results, not evidence of matching individual fires. The tool is designed to support exploration and situational context—not to confirm incidents, estimate burned area, or forecast fire risk.

Pyrochron is built in Python with Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, Altair, Folium and streamlit-folium. It uses NASA FIRMS for fire detections, NASA POWER/MERRA-2 for historical weather context, and Docker Compose to run the dashboard and API together.

The project’s creative focus is connecting a user-selected place and near-real-time observations with a transparent historical record in one interface. We considered differences between satellite sensors, changing coverage over time, data quality, seasonal variability, API limits and the uncertainty of provisional detections.
